narrative_purpose: Makes the astrobiology passage concrete: disciplined speculation may test unfamiliar chemistry, but carbon in liquid water remains the flexible benchmark while silicon tends toward rigid mineral lattices.
subject: A split naturalist laboratory plate with two sealed shallow glass dishes viewed side by side. In the left dish, dark bead-like atoms form many long branching flexible chains suspended and curling through clear liquid, with several chain ends joining and separating. In the right dish, pale stone-like atoms lock into a rigid repeating angular crystal lattice that grows into a small quartz-like solid and does not curl through the liquid. The two dishes are identical in size so the difference between flexible chains and a rigid mineral network is unmistakable.
scene: A dim astrobiology workbench with only the two dishes visible against dark slate; faint condensation beads cling to the glass and a few indistinct mineral grains lie beyond the right dish.
camera: Straight-down close comparison view, both circular dishes fully visible at equal scale.
light: Cool internal glow in the liquid dishes; the flexible chains catch a living teal edge, while the rigid crystal catches a restrained pale amber rim.
palette: Figure-specific contrast of living teal on the flexible chains and desaturated stone with a scarce amber edge on the rigid lattice, against the global dark ground.
style: Painterly naturalist laboratory plate with literal molecular-scale forms enlarged into visible bead-and-bond structures; not a textbook infographic.
detail_level: High detail on the branching chain geometry and the repeating angular crystal lattice; bench and background soft and sparse.
composition: Two equal dishes balanced left and right with a narrow strip of dark negative space between; the left is visibly fluid and branching, the right compact and immobile.
consistency_notes: The image must show a physical contrast, not merely two colored blobs: many flexible branching chains in liquid on the left, one rigid repeating stone lattice on the right.
negative_prompt: no text, no symbols, no periodic-table glyphs, no labels, no arrows, no UI, no glossy 3D molecular render, no photographic look, no clutter
